labels.FL-002: Memory units have a length cap; a memory over the cap is shortened to fit as one memory, and it is split only when it holds more than one distinct fact, with the split logged.
labels.FL-014: Every memory records the folder the agent stood in when it was made.
labels.FL-038: A cheap 80/20 duplicate check at memory creation, keeping the agent's memory work under 10% of build run time.
labels.FL-042: Constitution: 'Already known — reinforced' on re-saves; rejected candidates remembered and never re-proposed without material change (gate-day).
labels.FL-051: A performance score for the memory system, back-tested on the history of manual adds and removes plus successful injections; a new set of weights is accepted only if it scores better than the previous generation.
labels.FL-052: The scoreboard counts right and wrong injection decisions, injected or not, with no arbitrary scoring.
labels.FL-069: The core tools every modern harness has: files, terminal, Chrome, skills, changing models, compaction (our own take), and interactions with common apps, taken from the most modular standard source.
labels.FL-197: Spend and Palace state reads use the calling principal; only the configured owner can request the whole Palace.
labels.FL-187: Two repos, the spine (memory) and the Harness, not a mono repo.
labels.FL-190: The Harness can use skills and has the best and most common tools available, compiled from a list.
labels.FL-191: The tools and skills Claude Code and Codex use on this machine, pinned to versioned open-source sources.
labels.FL-194: The Pydantic toolset and skills as the tool layer.
labels.FL-195: The feature ledger generates coverage reports and requires evidence for the rows affected by a build.
labels.FL-196: The rules machine checks citations, frozen law, product vocabulary, seed states and packet precedents.
labels.FL-201: One scale across modules: an icon reused anywhere is one size, text of one role is one size and one font, and a box belongs only to an icon that is a button.
labels.FL-006: Every memory carries a location column and a project column.
labels.FL-007: Every memory links to the full conversation it came from, so an agent can reach more than just the memory when needed.
labels.FL-009: Record files (history, transcripts) live apart from code so code can be deleted and re-downloaded without losing history.
labels.FL-010: Every thread has a thread id, and every memory records the thread it was born in.
labels.FL-061: Compaction instructions tuned by back-test; memory size as a tunable beside the threshold and allotments.
labels.FL-080: Compaction triggered by fill percentage against the model's best working range and max, which vary by model.
labels.FL-084: Plan-mode compaction: the summarizer asks the user one to four questions before compacting. (seed SD-040)
labels.FL-137: A line graph of the injection system's historical performance; a 3D terrain of the score surface across parameters; the optimization shown while it runs (the landscape module is this terrain, placed beside the curators).
labels.FL-170: A fresh reinstall that reconnects to existing files and auto-finds the cloud palace.
labels.FL-186: Build on Pydantic AI in a way that lets us modify and extend without waiting on them, passing features back and forth with their library.
labels.FL-192: Swappable seams: router, model policy with an off-switch, toolset as a unit, memory system.
labels.FL-193: The common core of terminal-agent tools (skills, progressive prompting, model switching, compaction, app interactions) in one piece that pulls upstream updates.
